title.rendered: Once I Was Blind, Now I See: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see.” A morning devotional on the simplest and most powerful testimony in the Bible.

content.rendered:
“One thing I know. That though I was blind, now I see.” Twelve words. The simplest testimony in the New Testament, from a man who had been blind from birth, spoken back to the very religious authorities who were trying to intimidate him into denying what Jesus had done.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, September 10, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“He answered and said, ‘Whether He is a sinner or not I do not know. One thing I know: that though I was blind, now I see.'”
John 9:25 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

He had been blind from birth. Never seen his mother’s face. Never seen the sky. Never seen a Sabbath sunrise in Jerusalem. He begged at the entrance to the Temple, day after day, invisible to almost everyone who walked past him. And one Sabbath afternoon, Jesus stopped, spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the man’s eyes with the mud, and told him to go wash in the Pool of Siloam. He went. He washed. He came back seeing. And what followed was one of the most extraordinary and quietly heroic exchanges in the whole New Testament.

The religious authorities were furious. Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. They dragged the man in. They interrogated him. They tried to trap him. They demanded he denounce Jesus as a sinner. And the man, who moments before had been a lifelong beggar with no theological training and no social power, gave one of the most famous answers in Christian history. “Whether He is a sinner or not I do not know. One thing I know: that though I was blind, now I see.” Twelve words. The simplest testimony in the New Testament. And the most powerful defence any believer has ever offered.

The Passion Translation renders it with striking clarity: “The man answered, ‘I have no idea what kind of man he is. All I know is that I was blind and now I can see!'” (John 9:25 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Then he answered, I do not know whether He is a sinner and wicked or not. But one thing I do know, that whereas I was blind before, now I see” (John 9:25 AMPC). The man refused to argue theology. He refused to be pulled into a debate he could not win. He simply told them what had happened to him, in the plainest possible words, and let the fact of his healing speak for itself.

This is the model for every Christian testimony that has ever mattered. The believer does not need to have every answer to every objection. The believer does not need a PhD in theology to talk about Jesus. The believer needs to know what has happened to them, and be willing to say it plainly. The blind man could not explain the mechanism of his healing. He could not defeat the Pharisees in a Sabbath-law debate. What he could do was say, with complete clarity, “I was blind. Now I see.” That was enough. It threatened the whole religious establishment. It got him thrown out of the synagogue. And it drew Jesus back to him personally, in the very next paragraph, to reveal Himself to the man as the Son of God, and to receive the man’s worship.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is your permission. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you do not need to have every answer before you speak about Jesus. You do not need to win every argument. You do not need to hold a graduate degree in apologetics. You need to know what Jesus has done in your life, and be willing to say it plainly, without embellishment and without apology, to the people around you. I was blind. Now I see. That is the testimony that changes families, workplaces, neighbourhoods, and nations. Speak it today. The One who opened your eyes will honour the words you speak about Him.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has opened my eyes. I was blind and now I see. I do not need to have every answer to every objection to speak about Him. I do not need to win every debate. I need only to tell what He has done in my life, plainly and without apology. Today I ask You for the courage of the man born blind. Give me the plain words to say what Jesus has done for me, to whichever person You put in my path. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I was blind, and now I see. Jesus has opened my eyes. I do not need to win every debate. I need only to tell what He has done. And I will.
